en.title: All Ways to Complete a Weekly Schedule
en.description:
Replace each question mark in the seven-digit pattern with a value in 0..day_hours so that the weekly total is exactly work_hours. Fixed digits stay unchanged. Return all schedules in ascending lexicographic order. At least one valid schedule is guaranteed.

The input/output protocol was compiled independently by this site; upstream solutions are not executed.
en.input: The first line contains work_hours day_hours, and the second line contains the 7-digit pattern. 1≤work_hours≤56, 1≤day_hours≤8; the pattern consists of 0..8 or ?, and fixed hours do not exceed the daily limit. The original constraints omitted ?, which is restored from the body text.
en.output: First output the number of schedules R, then one 7-digit schedule per line; all schedules must be output in ascending lexicographic order.
en.explanation:
The answers to the three public examples are, in order: 3
0120000
1110000
2100000; 7
0000001
0000010
0000100
0001000
0010000
0100000
1000000; 1
8888888. All examples have been verified by independent small-scale enumeration or state search.
hints: Enumerate digits from left to right in ascending order, prune with the minimum/maximum remaining hours, and keep the leaves that hit the total exactly.
